question: EU law tells makers of baby biscuits what to add to curb acrylamide from browning. What?
options: An enzyme that breaks down asparagine
An antioxidant such as rosemary extract
Extra sugar to finish the bake sooner
answer: An enzyme, asparaginase. It turns asparagine, the amino acid that becomes acrylamide during browning, into aspartic acid, which cannot. In dough it can cut acrylamide by well over half without changing the bake. Regulation 2017/2158 made it the rule for baby biscuits: one ingredient of the reaction is gone before the oven is lit.
move: To stop an unwanted product, starve the reaction of its raw material.
trap: An antioxidant, the usual remedy for anything linked to cancer.
